Ziha
zī´hah
n. (head of a family of Nethinims, and their overseer in Jerusalem)
Hebrew Tsicha, of uncertain meaning. The name heads the list of the Nethinims — the given ones, temple servants assigned to the Levites for the menial work of the house of God.

Biblical Definition

When the exiles were numbered, a whole class of temple servants was counted, and this family stands first: “The Nethinims: the children of Ziha, the children of Hasupha, the children of Tabbaoth” (Ezra 2:43). Nehemiah's parallel register gives the same order: “The Nethinims: the children of Ziha, the children of Hashupha, the children of Tabbaoth” (Nehemiah 7:46). And when Jerusalem was resettled, the Nethinims were given a quarter and a head: “But the Nethinims dwelt in Ophel: and Ziha and Gispa were over the Nethinims” (Nehemiah 11:21). Their origin lies in David's reign and earlier — given, as the name says, to the service of the house: “Moreover David and the captains of the host separated to the service of the sons of Asaph, and of Heman, and of Jeduthun, who should prophesy with harps, with psalteries, and with cymbals” (1 Chronicles 25:1). The Nethinims did none of that. They drew water and cut wood and carried what needed carrying, and Ezra sent for some of them when he found no Levites among his returning company, because the house could not be served without them.

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster (1828) defines Nethinim as servants of the priests and Levites, appointed to the meanest offices about the temple; Ziha is a head of that order.

NETHINIM, n. plu. Servants given to the Levites for the inferior offices of the temple; the given ones.

ZIHA, n. The head of a family of the Nethinims, and an overseer of that order in Jerusalem.

OPHEL, n. A part of the hill of Zion at Jerusalem, where the Nethinims dwelt.

MENIAL, a. Pertaining to servants; low; mean; belonging to the humblest offices.

DEVOTE, v.t. To appropriate by vow; to set apart or dedicate by a solemn act; to consecrate.

Modern Corruption

Humble service is ranked below visible ministry, and a class of men Scripture counts by name and settles by neighbourhood is treated as beneath notice.

expand to see more

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. The principle to recover is that the house of God ran on labour nobody watched. The Nethinims — the word means the given ones — cut the wood and drew the water. They did not sing, teach, or offer. And Scripture counts them family by family in two separate registers, names their chief, and records the street they lived on. Ezra, gathering his caravan for the return, discovered he had priests and no Levites, sent back for ministers for the house, and came away with two hundred and twenty Nethinims, every one of whom, he says, was expressed by name.

The gospel takes that valuation and deepens it. Our Lord washed feet and said that he that is greatest among you shall be your servant; Paul insists that the members of the body which seem to be more feeble are necessary, and that God has given more abundant honour to the part that lacked. A church that ranks its members by visibility has adopted a scale the Bible nowhere uses. The man who unlocks the building is in the same register as the man who preaches in it, and in Nehemiah's case the register survives and the sermon does not.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Hebrew Tsicha (H6727), Ziha; Nethinim (H5411), the given ones; nathan (H5414), to give; Ophel (H6077), the hill quarter of Jerusalem.

expand to see more

Hebrew Tsicha (H6727) — Ziha, head of the first-listed Nethinim family.

Hebrew Nethinim (H5411) — the given ones; temple servants assigned to the Levites.

Hebrew nathan (H5414) — to give; the root from which their name is formed.

Hebrew Ophel (H6077) — the swelling or hill; the quarter where they dwelt.

Hebrew abodah (H5656) — service, labour; the work of the house of God.

Usage

"“The Nethinims: the children of Ziha” — first in both registers."

"“Ziha and Gispa were over the Nethinims” — their appointed heads."

"“The Nethinims dwelt in Ophel” — counted, named, and housed."
